candidates.title: Summarize agent runs each week

demandEvidence.chore: Schedule Trigger (weekly): summarize runs per agent for the team lead.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Schedule Trigger (weekly): summarize runs per agent for the team lead.

ease.reason: A weekly summary from agent runs is a bounded design, but the post supplies no implementation reference or input format.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a team lead might pay for a clearer agent-run summary; this community post does not establish a buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock could summarize supplied sample runs; the post gives no run schema or accuracy requirements.

autonomy.reason: A weekly trigger and summary are proposed; a person must verify source logs and investigate anything the summary flags.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly proposes a weekly summary of agent runs for a team lead, but not repeat use or implementation details.

candidates.reason: Below the 6-point threshold: the request gives a weekly summary task, but no run format, implementation reference, or validated buyer. The Make lead also proposes agent-run reporting, so it is assessed as the same workflow and buyer hypothesis.

candidates.title: Log agent runs to a Google Sheet

demandEvidence.chore: Every time an agent finishes or fails a task, Make should record the agent name, task ID, status and time in a Google Sheet.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Every time an agent finishes or fails a task, Make should record the agent name, task ID, status and time in a Google Sheet.

ease.reason: The post names a trigger, four fields, Make, and Google Sheets, but no attached reference documents their integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a team lead might pay for agent-run records; the request shows no paying customer or willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A test could record supplied sample events and the named fields in four weeks; authentication and failure handling are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed event-triggered record is repeatable, but a person must validate fields, permissions, and missing or incorrect events.

evidence.reason: The post specifies recording agent name, task ID, status, and time on each finish or failure, but offers no use results.

candidates.reason: Below the 6-point threshold. It overlaps the n8n assignment at https://community.n8n.io/t/323013: both are team-lead reporting of agent runs, despite distinct platforms and post URLs.

candidates.title: Send triggered email through Make

demandEvidence.chore: I want a Make scenario to send an email through DigitalAka when a trigger occurs in another app.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want a Make scenario to send an email through DigitalAka when a trigger occurs in another app.

ease.reason: A sample trigger and operator-controlled test inbox make a small test conceivable, but no attached reference documents the SMTP integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a business might pay for triggered-email setup; this request establishes neither a buyer nor willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test could use one sample trigger and test inbox; provider setup and delivery failures remain unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A test message could follow a trigger, while a person must approve recipients, content, and any real send.

evidence.reason: The post names a Make scenario, an SMTP provider, and an app trigger, but gives no configuration or successful result.

candidates.reason: Below the 6-point threshold: the post names a triggered email task, but no integration reference or delivery details support a dependable loop.

rejected.title: Faro Signal client
rejected.reason: The captured excerpt is only a Show HN product title for a terminal Signal client. It states no customer chore, request, or task to assess.

rejected.reason: The text says the author is working on how to add agents to Jira-like workflows but gives no concrete task or requested outcome. The title’s notification idea is not present in the supplied literal source text, so it cannot support a task assessment.

rejected.title: Guidance for a Make beginner

rejected.title: Engage a customer with a product story
rejected.reason: The question asks how to engage a customer in a product story but specifies no concrete task, repeatable input, or bounded output for a proposed service.

rejected.title: Independent chatbot evaluation experiences
rejected.reason: The post asks for firsthand experiences from people who hired an evaluator; it is research about prior service purchases, not a request for a concrete evaluation chore or tool. The underlying task is not described.

steps.message: Assessed all ten assigned discussion posts. Three concrete workflow requests received five provisional criterion scores; each is below the 6-point threshold. Rejected the other seven where the supplied excerpt lacked a concrete task, described a platform-access issue, or requested research rather than a bounded service.
